## UNIX Domain Socket Listener Support (PR #2701)

The most relevant pull request is **#2701** by John Millikin (jmillikin-stripe), which added UNIX domain socket listening support to Envoy. Since the Address protobuf type is already used for listener addresses, there was no API change, and both file-like and Linux's abstract socket addresses are supported. This PR fixed issues #1605 and #2697.

## UDP Listener Introduction (PR #5473)

The **UDP listener** was introduced in PR **#5473** by Jojy G Varghese (conqerAtapple). This PR contains discussion directly relevant to your query about datagrams over Unix domain sockets. Reviewers debated the naming and generality of the datagram handling — one reviewer wondered whether they would ever want to support proxying datagrams over Unix domain sockets in addition to over UDP (analogous to Envoy support for pipes vs. TCP connections), suggesting it might be more general to name it createDatagramListener, unless UDS datagrams weren't worth supporting.

Ultimately, the team decided to keep the "Udp" naming for consistency. One reviewer took back an earlier suggestion, noting that since everything else in the PR refers to "Udp," it seemed out of place and inconsistent to use "Datagram," so it was better to go with "Udp" as originally written.

- Constructor takes `Network::Address::IpVersion`, creates a loopback `UdpListenSocket` and sets it to blocking (`fcntl(..., F_SETFL, 0)`).
- `write(buffer, peer)` sends a datagram via `Network::Utility::writeToSocket` and asserts all bytes were sent.
- `recv(datagram)` synchronously reads one datagram via the existing `readFromSocket` wrapper.
- `localAddress()` returns a const ref to the socket's local address.
- Added `#include "common/network/listen_socket_impl.h"`.

**`source/extensions/stat_sinks/common/statsd/statsd.h` / `.cc`** — Reworked `UdpStatsdSink`:
- `Writer` is now a nested abstract class inheriting `ThreadLocal::ThreadLocalObject` with pure virtual `write(const std::string&)`.
- Added nested private `WriterImpl` concrete writer that creates a datagram socket for the server address and sends via `Network::Utility::writeToSocket` (no `connect()`).
- Dropping `connect()` is what enables **UDS support** and **graceful failure when no server is listening** — datagrams to an unbound peer simply fail silently instead of asserting at construction. Once a UDS/IP server binds and listens, flush delivers correctly-formatted statsd datagrams.
- Removed the old `getFdForTests()` accessors that no longer apply.
